source_images_viewed.observation: Title, all five authors (Xijun Hu, Lei Liu, Yuwei Ou, Pedro A. S. Salomao, Guowei Yu) and arXiv:2308.00338v1 1 Aug 2023 stamp agree with the report binding.

Equations (3.3),(3.7)-(3.9) display the c=m^(5/2)/sqrt(2) potential factor. The following sentence visibly replaces energy h by h*c while dividing angular momentum squared by c; this is the exact P2 location. Positive alpha/angular momentum and compact-level hypotheses follow in Proposition 3.1.

Remark 6.5 explicitly claims the specified canonical action-angle transformation makes the limiting energy surface strictly convex. It defines (x,y)=(sqrt(I/pi)cos(2pi phi),sqrt(I/pi)sin(2pi phi)) and h_u(pi(x^2+y^2)); the range h_u in (-4,0) and (6.13) are visible.

Figure 6.1 actually inspected: the K2 level-set plot and axes correspond to the limiting subsystem. The following h_u'' formula ends with a positive expression and the Hessian limit is printed 32 I_2, matching P1's target; the report distinguishes this from its actual boundary-point counterexample.

Lemma 8.2 and equations (8.8)-(8.10) show the separate finite-alpha curvature/stationary-branch argument, including the critical boundary/interior distinction used as counterevidence to broadening P1.

Figures 8.2 and 8.3 actually inspected. Delta sign regions and branches are labelled; the blue e_conv(beta) curve lies below the boundary-loss dashed curve and the physical-domain arc. Theorem 2.11 proof starts from separate Lemmas 8.5/8.6, matching the report's retained limitation.
The explicit beta_conv,e_conv,W,G parameterization, its domain and monotonicity expressions are visible and correspond to the reported finite-parameter coverage.
The e_conv'' computation and conclusion of Theorem 2.11 are visible; Appendix A's index definitions begin below. This is coverage correspondence, not a new proof of all imported index theory.
Appendix proof of Lemma 8.3 displays the discriminant quadratic, unique zero and smooth branch treatment at k^2=3/2, consistent with the retained coverage.
Claims B.1/B.2, the critical-point inequalities and W,G,W' expressions are visible. No independent new certification of every auxiliary inequality is inferred from this visual check.
